title: Celebrating the ASYV Class of 2026 and Our Alumni
excerpt: On May 15, the 128 members of our Ishami Grade, the ASYV Class of 2026, graduated. They joined ASYV's over 1,700 alumni building  Rwanda's future and thriving in industries from tech to sustainable agriculture to education.

title: The Young Entrepreneurs of ASYV
excerpt: Through ASYV’s Entrepreneurship Program, our students learn how to turn classroom lessons into businesses able to solve the most pressing problems Rwandans face. In this newsletter, we discuss he finalists for the 2026 ASYV Business Plan Competition, including a tutoring app, a mental health app, and smart glasses for the visually impaired. We also sit down with ASYV alum Kevine Kirezi, our current Science Center intern, to discuss her work sharing her passion for science with our students.

title: The Young Women of ASYV Leading Change
excerpt: Each March, we come together to mark Women’s History Month with performances, discussions, and campaigns. In this newsletter, we explore how our students inspire their younger ASYV sisters to pursue passions in fields like photography traditionally dominated by boys and the impact of our gender equity strategy. We sit down with ASYV graduate Julia Gihozo to discuss her career in Rwanda’s technology industry. And we showcase a student-made short film telling the story of one second-year student.

title: Stories of Students Thriving Through Creativity and Innovation
excerpt: Third-year student Ntihebuwayo Nehemie discusses discovering his love of cinematography in the Village. Fourth-year students Nyirakaneza Princess and Niyomukiza Pascal, tell us how they applied their chemistry know-how to developing a new, improved hand soap that impacted their community. Finally, we hear how our IRIS program is transforming how four refugee students see their futures.

title: Back to School! An Update from Our Students
excerpt: On September 6, we had the joy of welcoming our second-, third-, and fourth-year students back to the Village for the 2024–2025 school year. One week later, we welcomed our 128 Enrichment Year (EY) kids to the ASYV family. Read about our students’ goals and accomplishment and an update on the launch of our Ikaze Refugee Impact Scholarship program.

title: How Our Students Are Building A Thriving Future: Our New Report
excerpt: Each  day, when I enter the Village, the power of  our ASYV family inspires me. That power is reflected in Building a Thriving Future Together, our annual report covering the 2024–2025 school year. In the report, you'll find the voices of many of our family members, including students, alumni, and staff. You’ll find exciting updates about our program and impact.

title: How Our Kids Learned to Lead This Summer
excerpt: At ASYV, we work to help each student discover their passions and talents, then develop the skills they need to turn those interests into thriving careers. At the end of each school year, our Career Resources Center pairs interested students with summer opportunities that will help them get hands-on professional experience, learn about new cultures, and/or deepen their academic expertise. We sat down with several students to discuss their summer activities.

title: ASYV Alumni Discuss Their Careers and Future Dreams
excerpt: Our graduates are hard at work building thriving lives and a better future for Rwanda and the world. We recently sat down with three alumni to hear about what they’ve been up to since graduation and what they hope to do next. In addition, the graduates of our 2024 practical skills program are thriving in the work force. Learn more about their jobs and small businesses.

title: ASYV New York Leadership Update
excerpt: I’m writing to share some bittersweet news. After eight years, I am transitioning out of my role as ASYV’s Chief Advancement and Strategy Officer. My successor, Katie Messick, brings what the Village needs for its next steps. I can’t wait to see all she accomplishes.

title: Tulane Study Proves ASYV's Incredible Impact on Our Students
excerpt: Since our founding, we’ve had a vision for a better future—one in which our model can reach young people in need of healing, education, and love across Rwanda, the region, and one day, the globe. I’m thrilled to share that now, thanks to an analysis conducted in partnership with faculty and staff from the Tulane University, we’re close to making that dream a reality.

title: Kwibuka 32
excerpt: April began Kwibuka 32, the 32nd commemoration of the 1994 Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda. Our students created this video to honor the memory of the over one million Rwandans whose lives were brutally extinguished.

title: My First Months at ASYV
excerpt: I made this video because when a student arrives here at Agahozo-Shalom, they don’t know much about the Village. I wanted to show these students a few months into their time here—to capture the moment when they first understand all that we have here at ASYV, and how they can use those resources to improve their lives.

title: And the Winners Are...
excerpt: Three students who took a top prize during our annual ASYV photo competition explain their winning shots.

title: The Twist of Agahire: A Multimedia Collaboration
excerpt: Don’t miss "The Twist of Agahire," a poetry performance written, performed, produced, and filmed entirely by our talented students. The contributing student artists include poets Agahire Sharangabo Keira, Gashami Aisha, and Ntwali Christian; musician and singer Umutoniwase Bienveillance; and cinematographer Denny Ngoga.

title: An Original Poem: Nelson Mandela
excerpt: I remember sitting during family time in the Village, and everyone was talking about their role models. Four students mentioned Nelson Mandela, and I imagined how incredible it would be if he could return and see just how deeply his actions have inspired generations.

title: How I Learned to Think Critically for Peace
excerpt: I joined Critical Thinking For Peace in my first year at ASYV. In truth, I joined without knowing what the club does, but I found that I loved it. We learn about critical thinking and do Model United Nations. You learn a lot by putting yourself in others’ shoes, and trying to address the problem from the point of view of a certain country in a certain situation. You're embracing that empathy within you and that opens up your mind.

title: The Power of Leadership
excerpt: Growing up, I noticed that many individuals in my community were indifferent to the different behaviors around them, allowing negativity and chaos to go unchecked. This lack of guidance stirred something within me—I wanted to make a difference. I wanted to be the kind of leader who inspired others—not through authority, but through positive influence and genuine care

title: My Film Celebrating ASYV’s New Music Studio
excerpt: I’m a person who tries to showcase my ideas through filmmaking. I want to challenge myself creatively every single day. When I wake up, I just want to make the next step in the next video I'm producing. I was asked by JC, ASYV’s CEO, to film the recording studio opening because he wanted the best video, and that is what I tried to deliver.

title: Be the Change, Write Your Own Story
excerpt: The theme of the 2024 edition of the Liquidnet Student Magazine is “Be the Change, Write Your Own Story.” Expressing yourself through writing is powerful and liberating. Imagine crafting worlds, evoking emotions, and sharing ideas—all through words.

title: Seeing My Land of a Thousand Hills
excerpt: Before the Grand Study Tour, like most Rwandans, I would use the statement “a land of a thousand hills,” but I couldn’t imagine how a country like Rwanda, which is among the smallest in the world, could actually hold a thousand hills. By the time our bus approached the Western Province, I was very amazed.
